To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MOISES project has developed a new methodology to study symbolic sequences that is based in formal concepts.

(i) the use of a formal concept is a useful and effective way of constructing predictive and descriptive models of symbolic sequences (ii) the models constructed using formal concepts are useful and effective in a wide variety of applications (iii) the models are easy to implement (iv) the models can be used to construct models of symbolic sequences of arbitrary size (v) the models can handle symbolic sequences that have no obvious underlying structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formal properties of the models that we will develop, and their use in the construction and validation of predictive models for symbolic sequences.
the study of the properties of symbolic sequences and the development of formal models that describe and predict the behaviour of such sequences.
the study of formal models and their applications to the analysis and synthesis of symbolic sequences, and with the design of new models for this purpose.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this proposal will contribute to the theoretical development and empirical validation of the formal concepts of symbolic sequences and their use in the construction and validation of predictive and descriptive statistical models.

the project aims at the study of symbolic sequences, with the objective of developing new models and algorithms, and the empirical evaluation of these models in the context of real data, with a view towards their application in the area of information retrieval and data mining.
this project will provide the necessary theoretical and methodological tools to the study of the structure of symbolic sequences, and the development of predictive models and data compression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have studied the following aspects: (1) compression algorithms and their generalizations, (2) grammatical models (3) probabilistic models, (4) models for subsequences, (5) models for time series, and (6) empirical validation.
we will develop and study the formal properties of models that are used in the construction of symbolic sequences, and we will validate them with real data.
we will study and develop new formal concepts for the modelling and compression of symbolic sequences.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the study of symbolic sequences is a very important area in the development of artificial intelligence and that it has a great number of applications in the areas of natural language processing, data mining, and bioinformatics.
we have been able to develop a new approach to the problem of symbolic sequences that is based on the use of formal concepts.
the use of these models can be used to predict the future, and to understand the past.
